chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased: Is Salat (prayer) performed upon it without ablution? He said: Yes. It is merely Takbeer (exalting God), Tahmid (praising God), Tasbih (glorifying God), and Tahlil (declaring oneness), just as you say Takbeer and Tasbih in your house without ablution.
ai.seo_question: Does one need to perform ablution (wudu) before praying Salat al-Janazah over the deceased?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Salat al-Janazah is a prayer of praise (*salat al-hamd*) rather than a ritual prayer (*salat al-fard*) requiring specific physical postures, thus exempting it from the condition of wudu. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the essential pillars of prayer and the recommended conditions, allowing the deceased to be honored even by those in a state of minor impurity, reflecting the accessibility of this act of worship.
